subject: Economy & Budget
q: Who presented the Federal Budget FY2025-26 in the National Assembly?
explanation: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb presented both the FY26 and FY27 budgets.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: The Federal Budget FY2025-26 was presented on:
explanation: Presented 10 June 2025; passed on 26 June 2025.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the total outlay (total spending) in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: Rs17.573 trillion - about 7% less than the previous year.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the FBR tax target in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: Rs14.131 trillion, up about 18.7%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much was allocated for defence in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: Rs2.55 trillion, up about 20% after the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the fiscal deficit target in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: Fiscal deficit target 3.9% of GDP; primary surplus target 2.4%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the GDP growth target in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: Growth target 4.2%; actual growth came in at 3.7%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: Government employees got what pay rise in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: 10% pay rise; pensions rose 7%. In FY27 the salary rise was 7%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much was allocated for BISP in the Federal Budget FY2025-26?
explanation: Rs716 billion, up 21%. In FY27 it rose to Rs838 billion.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much was set aside for debt servicing (interest) in FY2025-26?
explanation: Rs8.207 trillion - almost as big as the whole FBR tax target.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: The Federal Budget FY2026-27 was presented on:
explanation: Presented 12 June 2026; the Economic Survey came a day earlier, 11 June 2026.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the total outlay in the Federal Budget FY2026-27?
explanation: Rs18.771 trillion, up from Rs17.573 trillion in FY26.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the FBR tax target in the Federal Budget FY2026-27?
explanation: Rs15.264 trillion - a record, about 17.6% above FY26.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much was allocated for defence in the Federal Budget FY2026-27?
explanation: Rs3 trillion, plus about Rs822 billion in military pensions.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the fiscal deficit target in the Federal Budget FY2026-27?
explanation: About 3.6% of GDP (Rs7.02 trillion); primary surplus target about 2%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the GDP growth target in the Federal Budget FY2026-27?
explanation: Growth target 4%; inflation target 8.2% average.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much was allocated for BISP in the Federal Budget FY2026-27?
explanation: Rs838 billion, up 17%, covering about 12 million families.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the Federal PSDP allocation in BOTH the FY26 and FY27 budgets?
explanation: Rs1 trillion in both years - a favourite examiner trap.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: The Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26 was presented on:
explanation: Presented 11 June 2026, one day before the FY27 budget.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the real GDP growth in FY26 according to the Economic Survey 2025-26?
explanation: 3.7% - below the 4.2% target but the highest in four years.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the size of Pakistan's economy in FY26?
explanation: Rs126.9 trillion = $452.1 billion, the largest in history.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was Pakistan's per capita income in FY26?
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much did overseas Pakistanis send home as remittances in Jul-May FY26?
explanation: $33.9 billion, up 9%; a record $4.3 billion came in April 2026 alone.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: Which is the biggest sector of Pakistan's economy?
explanation: Services, about 58% of GDP; agriculture grew 2.89%, industry 3.51%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: Who is the Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
explanation: Governor Jameel Ahmad; decisions are taken by the Monetary Policy Committee.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: At its peak, what was the State Bank policy rate?
explanation: 22% from June 2023 to April 2024; it then fell step by step to 10.5%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: What was the State Bank policy rate in October 2026?
explanation: 12%, after a 50 bps hike on 26 October 2026.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How much is 100 basis points (bps) equal to?
explanation: 100 bps = 1%. So a 100 bps cut takes the rate from 12% to 11%.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: Pakistan's current IMF programme is its which number programme?
explanation: The 24th IMF programme; the mission chief is Iva Petrova.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: How large is the IMF Extended Fund Facility (EFF) for Pakistan?
options: About $1 billion FY27 — outlay Rs18.771tr, FBR Rs15.264tr, defence Rs3tr, deficit 3.6%, growth 4%. Survey FY26 — growth 3.7%, economy $452.1bn, per capita $1,901, remittances $33.9bn. Policy rate: peak 22%, now 12%. IMF: 24th programme, EFF $7bn.
explanation: EFF: 37 months, about $7 billion, approved 25 September 2024.
source: Team Axiom, Pakistan Economy, Finance & Budget (Ch. 3)

subject: Economy & Budget
q: Which sector of Pakistan's economy is most likely affected by US tariffs?
explanation: Textiles and apparel are ~75-80% of Pakistan's exports to the US, so the textile sector is by far the most exposed to US tariffs.
source: PIDE, Apr 2025 / Minute Mirror tariff analysis

subject: Economy & Budget
q: The IMF approved a loan of ___ for Pakistan under its Resilience and Sustainability programme:
explanation: The IMF Executive Board approved a 28-month RSF arrangement of about $1.3 billion for Pakistan on 9 May 2025.
source: IMF / Business Recorder / Pakistan Today, May 2025
